page: Amazon Web Services c6gd.large is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 2.5 GHz AWS Graviton2 processor based on the ARM64 architecture. It features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs with no hyperthreading, utilizing the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 model. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio, and includes a bundled 118 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume. Network connectivity is rated at a 1 Gbps baseline.

Benchmark results indicate that the c6gd.large delivers average single-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1519.49. However, multi-core and memory performance are more constrained, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 3013.99 and a Passmark memory score of 814.63, both placing in the lower percentiles. Read-only memory bandwidth for large blocks is measured at 36.52 GB/sec, while write bandwidth is 18.33 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c6gd.large offers a resource-dense entry point for ARM-native applications requiring high-speed local storage without the overhead of network-attached volumes. The presence of the 118 GB NVMe SSD makes it suitable for workloads that benefit from low-latency scratch space. Appropriate workloads include lightweight database operations, ARM64 software compilation, static web serving, and development or testing environments.
